required_symbols.name: initialize_bricks
required_symbols.purpose: Define the requested layout while retaining the existing slot indexing and horizontal placement.

required_symbols.name: on_code_swap
required_symbols.purpose: Call initialize_bricks() to apply this level-layout change to the running game. Keep this as a call to the authoritative initializer; do not copy its loop into on_code_swap.

required_symbols.name: brick layout is deterministic
required_symbols.purpose: Prove representative edge and center coordinates, horizontal placement, and the complete brick count.

required_symbols.name: hot swap preserves active round
required_symbols.purpose: Prove brick repopulation and preservation of active gameplay state, including velocity.

invariants: Keep all 35 brick slots and the existing seven-column, five-row indexing.
Keep each brick's existing horizontal coordinate formula.
For this level-layout workflow, on_code_swap must call initialize_bricks() exactly once and must not duplicate brick initialization logic.
initialize_bricks may reset brick state and bricks_left, but on_code_swap must not reset ball, paddle, score, or round state.
acceptance: The layout oracle uses index 0 = (25, 60), index 3 = (271, 36), and index 34 = (517, 172), with bricks_left == 35.
The hot-swap test must not assume reset_round velocity values: assign ball_vx = 1.25 and ball_vy = -2.5 before the call, then compare against those exact values afterward.
Before on_code_swap, set bricks[0].alive = false and reduce bricks_left; afterward require bricks[0].alive and bricks_left == 35.
